config.instructions: NorthMES is built test first. Plan what the issue asks, at the scope it states. Plan one behaviour at a time: for each behaviour, one step writes its failing test (name the test file, the test name and why it fails before the change) and the next step makes that test pass with the smallest change. A last step may refactor with the tests green. Take the tests from the issue's Tests first section and build at the seam it names; the seam under Seam is agreed. Name the test that proves each acceptance criterion. Integration and end-to-end tests run against Postgres that @testcontainers/postgresql starts through packages/testing, so each test run brings its own database and needs no docker compose, shared database or .env file. SQL-level tests of RLS policies, constraints and the catalog are their own seam in packages/testing. Tests use the mocked AI provider. Put every file the steps touch in ownedPaths: test files, migrations, generated schema snapshots, codegen output and the lockfile next to a changed package.json. Follow the ADRs the issue links. Return needs_input with the question and two or three options when the plan needs a decision that neither the issue nor a linked ADR makes, or when the issue allows readings that lead to materially different plans; settle smaller gaps with the reading closest to the issue and state it in plan. Mention related work the issue does not ask for in plan as a follow-up, and keep it out of the steps. Keep shared docs (the root README, guides under apps/docs, ADR status) out of the steps unless the task is a docs task. Leave size out of the output: NorthMES plans in Flow mode, where tasks carry no size.

Review the plan as a test-first plan and report every finding you see, each with its severity. Blocking: a step that changes code before the step that writes its failing test; a step that covers more than one behaviour; an acceptance criterion with no named test; a test at another seam than the issue names; a database test planned outside packages/testing and Testcontainers; a plan that contradicts a linked ADR; ownedPaths that miss a test, migration, generated file or lockfile the steps change; a step for behaviour the issue does not ask for. No person approves this plan after you, and the planner cannot split it. Also blocking: more than 15 files in ownedPaths or more than 12 steps (the project's plan budget; change this text when the budget changes); a plan that needs a product, legal or design decision the issue does not record; a plan that adds a pattern the issue and the linked ADRs do not name, such as a new package, a new module, a new kind of migration or a new shared dependency. For those three, say in the finding that the task needs a person. Write one comment per finding, with path "plan".

Deliver what the issue and the approved plan ask, at the scope they state. Work test first, one behaviour at a time, in the order of the plan's steps. For each behaviour: write the test, run it with pnpm and see it fail for the expected reason, commit it with a subject that starts with test:, then write the smallest code that makes it pass, run the test to see it pass and commit. Refactor with the tests green. Change or delete an existing test only when the approved plan says that test is wrong. Run pnpm check before you finish. Run every command as git or pnpm from the repository root: integration tests start their own Postgres through packages/testing, and any other command, docker included, waits for a person's permission. When a generated file conflicts (lockfile, schema snapshot, codegen output), regenerate it with its command. Write the pull request title as a Conventional Commit for users, taken from the issue's Changelog line, for example feat(planning): ..., with ! for a breaking change, and make the description as long as the change needs. When you answer review comments from CodeRabbit or another reviewer, check each one against the issue and the linked ADRs as well, and cite the issue or the ADR in the answer's evidence when one of them decides it. Return needs_input with the question when the plan and the code allow readings that lead to materially different work; settle smaller gaps yourself and name the choice in the pull request description. Note follow-ups in the pull request description rather than opening issues.

Report every finding you see, each with its severity, covering correctness and the NorthMES rules. Blocking: an acceptance criterion the diff does not implement, or behaviour the issue did not ask for; a behaviour change without a test; a test that would pass without the change; code committed before its failing test where the plan put the test first; a database test outside the Testcontainers harness in packages/testing, or one that connects as a superuser; a new table without row-level security enabled and split policies (FOR SELECT on read_scopes, separate FOR INSERT, FOR UPDATE and FOR DELETE policies on write_scopes, rather than one FOR ALL policy), or without the audit trigger or an allowlist entry with a reason; a write that bypasses the command pipeline; a module that reads another module's tables; a contributed GraphQL field that is not nullable, or a root field without the module prefix; a web remote that bundles its own copy of a shared singleton; an interactive element without an accessible name; state shown by color alone; a color or size on a screen that is not a token; a change that contradicts a linked ADR. Release 1 enables row-level security without FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, so a table without FORCE is correct. No person reads the code after you, and the pull request merges by itself once CI and CodeRabbit pass, so a should_fix finding reaches the pull request only as a suggestion. Grade each finding as blocking when it must be fixed before this merges, or as follow_up when it belongs in another issue, and name that work.
